title: Retention triage & exec briefing playbook (QBR + save plays)
body:
Purpose:
To provide a compact, actionable playbook for identifying renewal risk early (pre-QBR), triaging customers, and executing escalation + save plays with clear owner/accountability. This doc is intentionally lightweight — use in QBR prep runbooks and SDR/CSE handoffs.

Scope / audience:
- CS Managers, AMs, Solutions Engineers, CSMs owning high-touch accounts.
- Sales/Account Execs for shared-run renewals and exec escalations.
- SRE/Platform if product incidents affect renewal.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
1) Use the Risk Signal Matrix to flag customers for 1-week escalation window.
2) Run the QBR prep checklist (shelf-ready slides + usage trends).
3) If at-risk, start Save Play A (technical remediation + credit + executive outreach) within 48h.
4) Escalate to Executive Briefing once Save Play A fails or customer asks for exec-level review.

Risk Signals (examples to auto-surface in tracker):
- Usage drop > 40% month-over-month on core endpoints.
- Spike in error rate or SLA misses (>=2 major incidents in last 30d).
- Billing disputes or sudden reduction in committed capacity.
- No-show for 2 consecutive QBR invites OR repeated feature requests ignored.
- Product signals: increased latency, model degradation flagged by Optimize alerts.
- Contractual triggers: upcoming data residency or compliance audit that we cannot meet.

Risk severity matrix (quick):
- Low: single minor signal; owner = CSM; action = monitoring + targeted outreach.
- Medium: 2 signals OR 1 operational incident; owner = CSM + AM; action = 7-day remediation plan + canary credit.
- High: revenue at risk (renewal < 60d) OR exec dissatisfaction; owner = CSM + AM + CS Manager; action = immediate Save Play A + exec escalation.

QBR Prep Checklist (minimal required artifacts):
- QBR slide deck draft (1-pager exec summary + 3 pages: usage, incidents, roadmap fit).
- Renewal health dashboard snapshot (last 90d tokens, latency, error rate, cost breakdown).
- Top 3 asks list from customer + internal feasibility notes.
- Open action tracker (Jira/Linear keys for any outstanding bugs).
- Proposed renewal options (standard, discount, term changes) and impact to ARR.
- Communication plan: who talks to whom and when.

Renewal Tracker columns (canonical CSV for automation):
- customer_id, account_name, ae, csm, renewal_date, term_value_usd, auto_renew, risk_level, signals_summary, last_qbr_date, next_qbr_date, open_actions_count, last_incident_date, suggested_play, owner, last_touch_date

Triage playbook (play library) - short forms:
- Preventative Play: "Usage Health Check"
  - When: 90 days pre-renewal or usage dip detected.
  - Steps: run ingestion + token profile, run Optimize suggestions, propose batching/quantization pilot, share cost projection.
  - Owner: CSM + Solutions Eng.

- Reactive Play: "Technical Save" (Save Play A)
  - When: Medium or High risk with technical cause (latency/errors).
  - Steps: 1) Escalate to SRE (incident triage) 2) Propose immediate hotfix / fallback model 3) Offer 1-month credit on impacted TTV 4) Schedule 48h follow-up demo.
  - Success criteria: latency back under SLA, incident regression < 10% in 14d.

- Commercial Play: "Renewal Flex"
  - When: Customer cites price/term as primary blocker.
  - Steps: Prepare 2 options (short-term discount or extended term incentive). Use approval matrix for discount thresholds.
  - Owner: AE + Rev Ops.

- Exec Escalation: "Partner Exec Briefing"
  - When: High risk OR customer requests exec involvement OR commercial negotiation stalls with >7d.
  - Steps: 1) Book 30–45m with customer execs and our VP CS/Head of Sales 2) Present 1-page problem statement + proposed commitments 3) If platform issue, include CTO/SRE pre-read.
  - Template subject line for outreach: "Request: Exec briefing to align on renewal and platform commitments"
  - Attachments: QBR 1-pager, incident timeline, remediation commitments, contract options.

Example save play flow (timeline):
- Day 0: Flag customer (auto from tracker or CSM) -> CSM opens "At-risk" folder and notifies AE + CS Manager.
- 24h: Initial outreach + diagnostic call scheduled.
- 48h: Save Play A execution (technical remediation + offering credit) + update ticket with artifacts.
- Day 7: Follow-up with customer; if unresolved escalate to Exec Briefing.
- Day 14: Decision checkpoint; if customer still considering -> present commercial options; if customer declines, start offboarding plan.

Escalation templates (copy + paste) - short:
- First escalation (to internal stakeholders):
  Subject: [Escalation] {account} — critical renewal risk
  Body: Hi team, {account} flagged HIGH risk due to {signals}. Renewal date {date}. Requested immediate support from SRE/Product. Current owner: {CSM}; suggested next step: {save play}. Details in tracker: {link}.

- Exec outreach email (to customer exec):
  Subject: Requesting brief exec sync on {account} partnership and renewal
  Body: Hi {ExecName}, hope you’re well. We value our partnership with {account}. We've identified a set of issues impacting the experience and would like 30m to align on an action plan and commitments from both sides. Proposed times: {times}. Attached: 1-pager with problem + remediation. — {CSM name}

Roles & responsibilities (rules of the road):
- CSM: owns triage, QBR prep, day-to-day save play execution.
- AE: commercial negotiations and approval for term/discount tradeoffs.
- CS Manager: approves escalations to execs and oversees resource allocation.
- Solutions Eng / SRE: owns tech remediation, root cause analysis.
- Rev Ops: pricing approvals, discounting governance.

KPIs to watch (for QBR + renewal decision):
- Renewal likelihood (CS score) % over time.
- Net churn risk: dollars at risk vs pipeline.
- Time to remediation (days from flag to fix).
- QBR satisfaction NPS or simple 1–5 rating.

Notes / open questions (TODOs):
- Add automation rules for raising "Medium" risk on billing disputes (ask Rev Ops for billing webhook).
- Define precise credit model (how many token credits per SLA breach) — Liaise with finance.
- Build a Confluence canonical page and link this doc (this is a working draft).
- Check with Legal before including any binding language in exec briefing slides.

Attachment checklist for QBR/escale folder (what to upload to GDrive):
- QBR deck (pptx)
- 90d usage CSV export
- Incident timeline (doc) + RCA links
- PR/feature notes if roadmap items promised.

Notes to self and style: keep play names short (1–3 words), include success criteria, always attach measurable remediation, and maintain a clear single owner for each step.

Revision history (brief):
- 2025-11-10: initial draft by Asha.
- 2026-01-22: added technical save play (Marcus Chen).
- 2026-03-01: editorial pass and escalation templates (Elena).

Unresolved: need sample completed tracker row and real-world example case study (from a prior save) — ask Priya to share redacted notes.

Links/refs (internal):
- Slack thread: #cs-qbr-template-discuss (see messages 20–40)
- Confluence draft ID: CS-Retention-Playbook-Page
- Jira example: CS-8421 (follow-up actions for ACME integration incident)

If you use this: copy to a new QBR prep folder for the account, run the tracker export, and assign owners within 24h.

-- end --
